character: Daybreak is the smallest institution in this directory and the one whose paperwork most rewards reading. The single most consequential fact is that it is not only BPPE-approved: its MA in Counseling with a Specialization in Marriage and Family Therapy has been accredited by COAMFTE since 05/01/2024, running through 05/01/2030, and COAMFTE's Fall 2024 action letter records that the Commission removed three previously-imposed stipulations and accredited the program "with no stipulations." Institutionally, Daybreak is accredited by TRACS — the Transnational Association of Christian Colleges and Schools, a faith-based *national* accreditor recognized by the U.S. Department of Education and CHEA — which reaffirmed it as a Category IV institution on April 28, 2025, effective July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2035. It is not regionally accredited (no WASC), and at $300 per quarter credit — $27,000 tuition for the 90 credits, or about $30,500 all-in across 10 quarters once books, registration and library fees are counted — it is also the cheapest route to a California MFT licence in this directory by a wide margin. California's BBS does not care: BPC §4980.36 accepts a degree "obtained from a school, college, or university approved by the Bureau for Private Postsecondary Education, or accredited by either the Commission on Accreditation for Marriage and Family Therapy Education, or a regional or national institutional accrediting agency that is recognized by the United States Department of Education" — Daybreak satisfies all three limbs independently, and BBS lists it as a qualifying program. Outside California the picture is different, and the school says so itself: its own catalog warns in capitals that the MFT programs "MAY NOT sufficiently cover the MFT licensure requirements in other states or provinces," and it separately discloses that it has "no articulation agreement with any other college or university" and that its degree "may not be accepted by any other college or university as a basis for admission to a graduate-level program." Daybreak also "does not participate in federal or state financial aid programs" — no Pell, no Direct Loans, no Cal Grant. Every dollar of that $27,000 is cash or private credit.

What the school is actually built around is couple and relational work, and this shows up in the requirements rather than the brochure. The core theory course is not a generic survey but CFT 7000, which teaches a single named in-house model, IPCST (Internal Parent-Child Systems Therapy). Couples Relationship Therapy (CFT 6030) is a standalone required course sitting in the second term of Year 1, before most programs have introduced couples at all. The practicum requirement is where the commitment becomes measurable: 300 direct client-contact hours of which at least 100 must be *relational* — defined as conjoint work with "two or more individuals... who share an ongoing relationship beyond that which occurs in the therapeutic experience itself." California's BBS floor is 225 hours with no relational minimum, so Daybreak is requiring a third more hours and imposing a relational quota the state does not. The institution is formally affiliated with the Imago International Training Institute; Imago is required in the general MAC and IRT tracks (not in the MFT specialization) and IRT 9400, Advanced Imago Relationship Therapy Training II, is one of only four MAC electives. Daybreak is also an AASECT Organizational Provider, and Human Sexuality Education I is a required MFT course rather than a workshop.

Two contexts a prospective student should have plainly. First, this is a Christian institution in more than name: the catalog's MAC admissions list requires a "Signed Faith Statement," students are told "it is expected that students regularly attend and be involved in a local church," and Spirituality and Psychotherapy is one of the four MAC electives. Second, it was founded out of a Korean counseling lineage — president Dr. Jay Oh is the founder of the Korean Association for Marriage and Family Therapy and a former associate professor at Soongsil and Baekseok Universities in South Korea — and BPPE has approved every Daybreak program in Korean as well as English. The program's own published demographic table shows 30 of 35 MA students are Asian. Serving a specific linguistic and faith community well is a legitimate thing for a school to do, and Daybreak does it openly. The countervailing facts are also public and should be weighed honestly: the BPPE 2024 annual report gives the MA program a 21.28% completion rate, 26 degrees awarded, 0 of 26 graduates employed in field, and zero graduates sitting the LMFT exam in either 2023 or 2024; the COAMFTE outcomes table lists every accredited-era cohort (2023–2024 onward, 11 to 22 students each) as "IP — In Process," meaning no graduation, job-placement or licensure rate has yet been published for any cohort under accreditation. There is, as of this writing, no outcome data demonstrating that people finish this program and get licensed. Enrollment is also restricted: the MFT program page states Daybreak "currently accepts applicants residing in California and Maryland."
orientation: Systemic couple-and-relational therapy, taught through a named in-house model (IPCST) with a formal Imago Relationship Therapy affiliation, inside a Christian institutional frame

signature.title: Counseling and Psychotherapeutic Theories and Techniques: IPCST
signature.desc: "This course covers the integrative therapy model, IPCST: Internal Parent-Child systems Therapy. This therapy model is consistent with current professional research and practice, development of a personal model of counseling, and multidisciplinary responses to family, couples, and individual therapy."
signature.why: Most programs' required theories course is a comparative survey of the major schools; Daybreak's teaches one proprietary model by name. IPCST is not a recognised model outside this institution, so a student should ask directly what the evidence base is and how portable the training is — but it does mean the program has an actual theoretical spine rather than an eclectic shrug. The comparative survey is delivered separately, in CFT 6020 Advanced Marriage and Family Therapy.

signature.title: Couples Relationship Therapy
signature.desc: "This course is designed to help students learn the concepts and approaches of marital/couples therapy models. Coursework will also include assessment, treatment planning, and intervention of couple relationships. Throughout the class discussion, ethical issues and couples interventions with diverse populations, including working with interface issues of culture, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, disabilities and SES will be explored."
signature.why: A full required course dedicated solely to couples, scheduled in the Winter term of Year 1 — before the student has taken psychopharmacology, assessment, or law and ethics. Many California MFT programs fold couple work into a general family therapy course or leave it to an elective. Placing it this early is the clearest structural signal that this is a couples program that also licenses MFTs, rather than the reverse.

signature.title: Human Sexuality Education I
signature.desc: Covers sexual anatomy and physiology, sexual disorders, normative age-related sexual changes, response cycles, sexual interviewing technique, sexuality research and the history of sexology; also "alternate forms of sexual expression, creating a safe and ethical environment for treatment... possible impacts of disability on the experience of sexuality, and the self of the therapist."
signature.why: California requires human sexuality content for licensure, but most programs meet it with a short module or a weekend. Here it is a full required course backed by real institutional infrastructure — Daybreak is an AASECT Organizational Provider and runs an entire Human Sexuality and Sex Therapy specialization, including a Sexual Attitude Reassessment (SAR) course. An MFT student can take further HST courses as electives.

signature.title: Advanced Imago Relationship Therapy Training II
signature.desc: "This course covers Imago Relationship therapy with regard to affairs, crisis couples, and neurobiology. Using the principles of interpersonal attunement and intrapersonal attunement provide a map of the terrain that needs to be covered when working with couples in crisis."
signature.why: One of only four electives available to MAC students, and the point at which Daybreak's Imago affiliation becomes available to an MFT-track student. Imago is a specific, brand-name couples method (Harville Hendrix and Helen LaKelly Hunt); Daybreak is officially affiliated with the Imago International Training Institute and its president is a certified Imago clinical instructor. Note carefully: IRT 7000 Foundations of Imago is required in the general MAC and the IRT specialization, but is NOT on the MFT specialization's required list — an MFT student reaches Imago through electives, not by default.

signature.title: Carl Rogers Seminar
signature.desc: "The person-centered therapy of Carl Rogers is the focus of this seminar... Students also observe and participate in Rogerian counseling dyads. In the dyads students work on individual issues and therapy promotes their personal growth and counseling skills."
signature.why: A rare experiential elective: students are not only studying person-centred theory but doing therapy on their own material in supervised dyads for credit. Very few California MFT programs still require or offer graded experiential self-work of this kind, and for a fully-online program it is a notable choice — it means real personal exposure to classmates over Zoom.

signature.title: Spirituality and Psychotherapy
signature.desc: "This course is designed to provide information on spirituality and provides students with a holistic approach to understanding self and community through a spiritual focus... Students will be exposed to spiritual development models, spirituality and health research, and contemplative practices."
signature.why: Listed as one of the four MAC electives, this is where the institution's Christian identity becomes coursework rather than atmosphere. Worth reading alongside the required "Signed Faith Statement" in the admissions list and the expectation that students "regularly attend and be involved in a local church." The course description itself is framed broadly (spiritual development models, contemplative practice) rather than doctrinally; a separate CFT 9350 Christian Counseling exists but is not a MAC elective.

curriculum.note: Cohort-based and lockstep, on a four-quarter year with 10-week terms; classes meet twice a week for three hours, delivered by live Zoom (asynchronous, hybrid and in-person options also exist). The published full-time route is 2.5 years / 10 quarters; a 5-year part-time route runs the same courses at one per term. The sequence below is the 2.5-year full-time MFT track from the 2025–26 MFT Program Handbook, which supersedes the 2024–25 catalog by splitting practicum into CFT 7900B and an optional CFT 7900A. Note that the 90 units are QUARTER credits — the catalog states this is "Equivalent to 60 Semester Credits," so this is a 60-semester-unit degree, not a 90-semester-unit one. Students must earn at least 75% of credits at Daybreak and finish within 5 years.

practicum.starts: Year 2, Fall term — but gated: students are evaluated through the Practicum Preparation Process (PPP), which begins after three completed courses and must be finished by the end of the sixth course, "to determine my clinical readiness to work with clients... before I can enroll in my first practicum course."
practicum.hours: 300 direct client-contact hours, of which at least 100 must be relational (conjoint couple/family work), plus 100 supervision hours of which at least 50 must be based on raw data (audio or video). Group supervision capped at 8 people, individual at 2. Must be enrolled in practicum for at least 12 months. California's BBS floor under BPC §4980.36 is nine quarter units and 225 hours, so Daybreak requires materially more.
practicum.clinic: Daybreak University Child, Couple, and Family Therapy Center (DBU-CFTC), whose counseling services are operated by the International Institute for Couple and Family Relationships (IICFR)
practicum.detail: This is the question that decides everything for an online program, and Daybreak's own documents answer it in two directions that a prospective student must reconcile before enrolling. The handbook's "Beginning Requirements" list starts with "Obtained a trainee position at the Daybreak University Couples and Family Therapy Center (CFTC)," and requires a signed Affiliation Agreement to the Clinical Director only "if a trainee practices outside of the Daybreak University CFTC" — which reads as school-placed by default. But the Student Acknowledgement the student must sign says the opposite in plain terms: "I understand it is my responsibility to secure an appropriate clinical training site and qualified local supervisor (AAMFT Approved Supervisor or State-Approved supervisor)... failure to find a qualified site or supervisor will make completion of the program impossible." Ask admissions, in writing, whether a CFTC trainee slot is guaranteed. Mechanically: weekly Daybreak faculty group supervision by Zoom while actively seeing clients, plus weekly supervision at the local site; sessions must be video-recorded for supervision with client consent; hours tracked in TheraNest; proof of professional liability insurance and AAMFT membership required before any clinical contact; BBS Weekly Summary of Hours signed by the supervisor each week. The CFTC states its services are delivered by master's and PhD trainees "under the supervision of California-licensed Marriage and Family Therapists, in compliance with applicable California law and California Board of Behavioral Sciences requirements." Clinical supervisors may not continue a student in practicum: each quarter supervisors conduct a Practicum Review and a student may be required to discontinue practicum pending a remediation plan.
practicum.model_evidence: The University has its own on-site counseling center, in Southern California, so you can gain real world experience and practice counseling both individuals and couples while learning to help them navigate their life challenges.
practicum.model_why: Has an on-site counseling center and says time there counts towards the requirement, but never says every student trains there or that a seat is assured. Owning a clinic is not a placement model.

admissions.cohort_size: Very small and growing. The COAMFTE Graduate Achievement Data table gives exact entering cohorts for the MA MFT program: 2023–2024, 5 full-time + 6 part-time (11); 2024–2025, 13 FT + 7 PT (20); 2025–2026, 17 FT + 5 PT (22). Institution-wide, BPPE reported 193 students enrolled in 2024 across all programs, 126 of them at master's level.
admissions.prereqs: Baccalaureate degree in any major from an accredited college or university; cumulative GPA of 3.0 (lower considered on strength of overall application); no prerequisite coursework. Three-page double-spaced purpose statement, two letters of reference, admission interview, proof of ID, $100 non-refundable application fee. The catalog's MAC admissions list also requires a "Signed Faith Statement." TOEFL 550 PBT / 79 iBT unless the applicant holds a bachelor's from an accredited US or Canadian institution. Two hard restrictions: the MFT specialization is "limited to the residents of United States and Canada," and the MFT program page states Daybreak "currently accepts applicants residing in California and Maryland."
admissions.gre_evidence: Cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 (lower GPAs will be considered based on strength of overall application)

voices.text: "Take any advice I have with a grain of salt, but if the program is accredited, that's a decent sign. The challenge is finding people associated with the program on sites like LinkedIn... Not finding faculty or alumni profiles through a place like LinkedIn would give me pause."
voices.who: Mr.Smile12 (admissions advisor, verified faculty member), Student Doctor Network, 27 Nov 2024

voices.text: "Unless you are going there explicitly for the christian stuff, I'd say avoid it and find a reputable public university near you... I would be instantly suspicious of a resume that came across my desk with 'daybreak university' listed on it."

The original poster found the program through the COAMFTE directory while working full time, and was drawn by "evening/online/hybrid classes" and tuition that was "reasonable" — the exact trade the program is built to serve.

"I went to the California Government Boards of Behavioral Sciences website and looked up every school with MFT programs and compared each one. Daybreak University was the only online program that was affordable, and flexible."
voices.who: Erika Schweizer, MA MFT licensing-track student — testimonial published by Daybreak University on its own marketing page, so read it as promotional rather than independent

gaps: No freely-licensed photograph of Daybreak University or its Anaheim building exists on Wikimedia Commons (searched Commons file namespace for 'Daybreak University Anaheim' and the State College Blvd address). photo is null rather than hotlinking a copyrighted university image.

No 2026–27 academic catalog is published. The newest catalog found is 2024–2025 (effective 1 Jan 2024 – 31 Dec 2025), retrieved from the BPPE document server; the MFT Program Handbook is labelled 2025–2026 on the website but its own page footers still read 'MFT Program Handbook 2023', so some handbook content may be stale.

The catalog and the 2025–26 handbook give two DIFFERENT descriptions for HST 6000 Human Sexuality Education I — the handbook's text is the one the catalog assigns to HST 6100. The handbook version is used here; which is current was not resolvable.
Course descriptions carry no credit-hour, prerequisite or contact-hour detail per course, and there are no syllabi, reading lists or instructor assignments published anywhere public.

Whether a trainee position at the in-house CFTC is guaranteed to every MFT student, or whether students routinely have to find their own outside site, is genuinely ambiguous: the handbook's Beginning Requirements and its Student Acknowledgement point in opposite directions. Not resolvable from published documents.
No published application deadline; the academic calendar implies quarterly Fall/Winter/Spring/Summer starts but no cut-off dates were found.

No licensure exam pass rate exists. The COAMFTE Graduate Achievement Data table marks graduation, job-placement and licensure rates as 'IP — In Process' for every cohort since accreditation (2023–24, 2024–25, 2025–26), and BPPE's 2024 report records zero graduates sitting the LMFT exam in 2023 or 2024. There is therefore no outcome evidence either way.

The BPPE 2024 figures (21.28% MA completion rate; 0 of 26 graduates employed in field) are stark, but BPPE completion-rate methodology and how Daybreak computed the denominator were not verifiable, and a 0% in-field employment figure alongside 26 degrees awarded may reflect non-reporting rather than reality. Treat as a question to put to the school, not a settled finding.

No Reddit, GradCafe, Niche or GradReports discussion of Daybreak was retrievable (Reddit's search endpoint refused automated access; no results surfaced elsewhere). The only independent discussion found anywhere is the single Student Doctor Network thread, which has four posts and no one with first-hand experience of the program.
Whether Daybreak has ever sought or been denied WSCUC (WASC) regional accreditation is not addressed in any public document found.
What TRACS 'Category IV' designates was not confirmed from a TRACS source; the April 2025 Commission actions page records the reaffirmation but does not define the category.
The exact founding date of the institution and of the MFT program is not stated in the catalog or on the About page.

cost.per_unit: $300 per quarter credit (Master of Arts in Counseling)
cost.all_in: Catalog estimate $30,500 for the full program = $3,050 per quarter × 10 quarters, comprising $2,700 tuition + $300 books and supplies + $20 non-refundable registration + $30 refundable library/IT fee. Plus a $100 non-refundable application fee.
cost.financial_aid: None. "Daybreak University does not participate in federal or state financial aid programs" — no Title IV (Pell, Direct Loans), no Cal Grant, no VA benefits, no WIOA, confirmed by the BPPE 2024 annual report. A limited number of internal scholarships is available to full-time students with a 3.0+ GPA, awarded by a faculty committee each quarter.

exam.period: July 2018 - December 2024, pooled (13 semiannual BBS reports)

outcomes.as_published: Licensure rate is the percentage of graduates from the cohort year that have achieved ANY level of MFT licensure. For Master's programs only, COAMFTE has established a benchmark of 70% licensure rate for each cohort.
outcomes.access_note: Daybreak was accredited on 1 May 2024, so seven of its cohorts predate accreditation and the three since have no completers yet. It also published the COAMFTE template with the placeholder brackets still in the title. There is nothing to report here yet, which is what a newly accredited programme should look like.
outcomes.school_note: PUBLISHES THE TABLE BUT IT CONTAINS NO OUTCOME NUMBERS AT ALL. Accredited 05/01/2024, so the seven cohorts 2016-2017 through 2022-2023 are marked 'NOT ACCREDITED' and the only three cohorts with enrolled students (2023-2024 through 2025-2026) are all 'IP' (In Process) across every metric. Enrollment counts are given (FT 5/13/17, PT 6/7/5) but not one graduation, job placement, or licensure figure exists. Daybreak MUST NOT appear in a comparison table with a number in it - it has none. It has also left the COAMFTE template's placeholder brackets in the published document ('Graduate Achievement Data for [MA in Counseling with a Specialization in Marriage and Family Therapy]', 'Accredited: [05/01/2024]'), and published the full multi-page COAMFTE instructions-to-programs boilerplate along with the table.
